title: Israel in Ancient Days
description: Israel in Ancient Days in Tonic Solfa to DARWALL, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: William Cowper wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book I, hymn 132, “Old-Testament gospel Heb 4:2”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Hallelujah Metre (6.6.6.6.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to DARWALL; any other Hallelujah Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Is-rael in an-cient days, Not on-ly had a view Of Si-nai in a blaze, But learned the gos-pel too: The types and fig-ures were a glass In which they saw the Sa-vior's face.

lines: The types and figures were a glass
In which they saw the Savior's face.
Would teach the need of other blood,
The Lamb, the Dove, set forth
For he who can for sin atone,
Must have no failings of his own.
Was to be seen no more:
In him, our Surety seemed to say,
And by a Savior's death discharged.
O grant that I may faithful be
To clearer light, vouchsafed to me.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: William Cowper died in 1800.
credits: Words by William Cowper (1731–1800), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to DARWALL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
